2020.seasonRecap: Shash's Digestive Trubiscuit turned in one of the most dominant regular seasons the league has seen, storming to a 13-1 record and a league-best 2055.9 points before finishing the job with a 196.0-point explosion over Elvis in Week 17 to claim the title. Elvis's Alvin and the Chipmunks earned the runner-up spot at 8-6, riding the arm of Tyreek Hill's monster 57.9-point Week 12 outing along the way. Arthur and Max rounded out the playoff field, both landing at 8-6 in a tightly bunched middle. Iain provided the season's fireworks, posting the year's high with 201.28 points in Week 4, while Farhaan won the closest game of the year by a razor-thin 0.12 over Datta in Week 6. At the bottom, Datta's AndyReid's Stache limped to 2-12, and Dan endured Arthur's 115.16-point Week 12 beatdown, the biggest blowout of the season.

2021.seasonRecap: The 2021 season was a logjam at the top, with five different teams finishing 9-6 and the tiebreakers doing most of the heavy lifting. Farhaan's Corda-real-deal Patterson edged out the crowd on the strength of a league-best 2408.6 points for, then closed the deal in the postseason to take the title over Dan's Shanahanigans. It wasn't all smooth sailing for the champ — Ben dropped a season-high 243.44 points on Farhaan in Week 5, a 113.87-point blowout that stands as the biggest beatdown of the year. The closest call came in Week 11, when Varun slipped past Elvis by an absurd 0.02 points, while Elvis and Datta anchored the bottom of the table despite Elvis putting up a respectable 2132.2 PF. Max got the individual highlight of the season when Jonathan Taylor exploded for 53.4 points in Week 11, but it was Farhaan hoisting the trophy when the dust settled.

2022.seasonRecap: The 2022 season was defined by parity and chaos, with a logjam of teams finishing 8-6 and only slim margins separating the contenders. Iain's Reverse Cowgirls led the league in scoring (1872.1 PF) and posted the season's highest single-week total — a monstrous 206.70 in Week 4 — yet still had to settle for the No. 5 seed. Dan's 50 shades of Trey put up the most points among the top seeds, but it was Elvis's Swiss family Robinson who navigated the field despite a middling 8-6 record and 1730.8 PF that nearly matched his points against. In the end Elvis claimed the title over Max's TyreeksDaycare, who had cruised through the regular season on the strength of the year's biggest blowout — an 89.68-point demolition of Arthur in Week 8. Farhaan and Varun brought up the rear at 3-11 apiece, proving somebody has to lose in a league this crowded.

2023.seasonRecap: The 2023 season was a study in the gap between regular-season dominance and playoff glory. Shash's Josh Downs Syndrome bulldozed the league with a 10-4 record and a league-best 1894.0 points, but it was Dan's Livin La Vida Bosa — a barely-.500 outfit at 7-7 that squeaked into the playoffs — who caught fire when it mattered, taking down runner-up Ben's BryceSpice for the title. The scoring peaks were spectacular: Max dropped a season-high 180.78 in Week 3, and Varun rode Ja'Marr Chase's 52.2-point explosion in Week 5. Margins ran the full gauntlet too, from Iain edging Shash by a razor-thin 0.18 in Week 6 to Karvin burying Elvis by 89.26 in Week 13. Elvis's Swiss family Robinson brought up the rear at 3-11 with a league-low 1165.9 points, while Karvin's DannyDimes quietly posted the stingiest defense in the league. In the end, the trophy went not to the best team on paper, but to the one that got hot at the right time.
